note: Pass 1: agent-compiled per METHOD.md source hierarchy. Medium/low items await verification pass 2.

countries.name: Afghanistan

livingLanguages.note: ≈40 living; figure moves with Pashtayi/Nuristani split treatments

languages.name: Dari
languages.notes: Constitution Art.16 names Pashto + Dari official. Post-2021: no new constitution; Dari remains official in practice alongside Pashto.

ekguru.recommendation: Dari (prs) and Iranian Persian (fas) are mutually intelligible standards; ONE Persian course can serve both with notes.

languages.name: Pashto
languages.notes: Constitution names one 'Pashto'; ISO 639-3 splits Southern (pbt, Kandahar), Northern (pbu) and Central (pst, Wardak). Registry code 'pus' is ISO 639-2 collective, not 639-3.

ekguru.recommendation: recommended-pack; Southern (pbt) base with Northern notes.

languages.name: Southern Uzbek
languages.notes: Named in Art.16 ('Uzbeki') with official standing in Uzbek-majority areas. Distinct code from Northern Uzbek (uzn vs uzs).

ekguru.recommendation: watch — Turkic cluster candidate after Turkish/Azerbaijani.

languages.name: Turkmen
languages.notes: Named in Art.16 ('Turkmeni').

languages.name: Balochi
languages.notes: Macrolanguage 'bal': Afghanistan variety mostly Western Balochi (bgn). Speaker estimate uncertain; sources range 200k–1M.

languages.name: Pashayi languages
languages.notes: Constitution names one 'Pashayi'; ISO splits four (NE aee, NW glh, SE psi, SW psh). Dardic group, Laghman/Kapisa/Kunar valleys.

languages.name: Nuristani languages
languages.notes: Constitution names one 'Nuristani'; actually a BRANCH (Ashkun ask, Kamkata-viri bsh, Prasuni prn, Tregami trm, Waigali wbk). Group entry per METHOD, not a language.

languages.name: Pamiri languages
languages.notes: Constitution names one 'Pamiri'; Eastern Iranian cluster (Shughni sgh, Wakhi wbl, Munji mnj, Yidgha ydg, Ishkashimi isk, Sanglechi sgy). Below threshold individually; constitutionally named so listed as group.

languages.name: Standard Arabic
languages.notes: Quranic/madrassa Arabic; no L1 community. Classical vs Modern Standard treatment varies; 'arb' is the collective standard code.

ekguru.recommendation: Covered by MSA Arabic course notes; no separate action.

languages.name: Afghan Sign Language
languages.notes: Treatment uncertain: no distinct ISO 639-3 code established; may share Kabul variety with broader regional signing. Verification pass 2 must confirm against WFD/deaf-org sources.

countries.notesLongTail: Below-threshold/notes-only: Kyrgyz kir (Wakhan, ~2–3k), Gujari gju (Kunar, small), Brahui brh (south, small), Mogholi mhj (moribund). English: working language of NGOs/government-in-exile circles, no official status.

countries.name: Bangladesh

languages.name: Bengali
languages.notes: Constitution Art.3: Bangla is the state language. Ekushey February (Language Martyrs' Day) origin country.

languages.name: English
languages.notes: Used in higher judiciary, higher education, business. NOT a constitutional official language — a common misstatement. No L1 community of note.

languages.name: Chakma
languages.notes: Largest CHT indigenous language; own script (Chakma/Ojhopath). Indo-Aryan despite Tibeto-Burman neighbours.

ekguru.recommendation: watch — largest stateless-script community in BD.

languages.name: Marma
languages.notes: Arakanese-related (Burmish); CHT. Estimates 150–350k.

languages.name: Rakhine
languages.notes: Arakanese of Cox's Bazar coast. Marma (rmz) vs Rakhine (rki) split follows Ethnologue; mutual intelligibility debated — note, don't merge.

languages.name: Kokborok
languages.notes: Tripuri; larger community across the border in Tripura, India. Cross-border entry — see IN notes.

languages.name: Santali
languages.notes: Munda (Austroasiatic); Ol Chiki script. Larger community in India where it is 8th-Scheduled.

ekguru.recommendation: recommended-pack (shared with India — one Santali pack serves both).

languages.name: Garo
languages.notes: A'chik; larger community in Meghalaya, India.

languages.name: Sadri
languages.notes: Tea-garden lingua franca (Sylhet); Oraon/Sadri identity. Code 'sck' treatment medium-confidence; verify pass 2.

languages.name: Urdu
languages.notes: Bihari/Stranded Pakistani community (Dhaka camps, Saidpur). Citizenship partly resolved 2008; statelessness persists for many.

languages.name: Rohingya
languages.notes: Refugee population (Cox's Bazar camps), not citizens; role 'minority' fits better than 'immigrant' (involuntary). Hanifi Rohingya script exists. Politically sensitive — keep entry factual.

ekguru.recommendation: watch — humanitarian-learner demand exists; needs native-speaker partnership, not agent authorship.

languages.name: Standard Arabic
languages.notes: Quranic/madrassa Arabic; no L1 community.

ekguru.recommendation: Covered by MSA Arabic course notes.

languages.name: Bangladeshi Sign Language
languages.notes: No distinct ISO 639-3 code; related to Indian/Pakistani signing (shared ISL-family). Whether BdSL is a distinct language vs ISL dialect is disputed — do not code as 'ins'. Verify pass 2 (WFD).

countries.notesLongTail: Below-threshold/notes-only: Khasi kha (~30k), Hajong haj (~50k), Bishnupriya bjy (~50k), Khumi, Mro, Pangkhu, Tanchangya tct (~20k; own script), Manipuri mni (Sylhet, small). Hindi/Urdu widely understood via media (not listed — no community).

countries.name: Bhutan

livingLanguages.note: DDC lists 19; Ethnologue/Glottolog counts differ by split treatment

languages.name: Dzongkha
languages.notes: Constitution: Dzongkha is the national language. L2-heavy (lingua franca of administration/education).

ekguru.recommendation: recommended-pack — national language, small authoring surface (phrases + script intro) serves real tourist/heritage demand.

languages.name: Tshangla
languages.notes: Largest MOTHER TONGUE (east); often wrongly called a Dzongkha dialect — it is a distinct Bodish language. Sharchopkha = same language, do not double-count.

languages.name: Nepali
languages.notes: Lhotshamkha (southern Bhutan). Individual code npi; India's scheduled entry uses macro 'nep' — same language, see IN notes (rule 12: no silent merge, no false split).

languages.name: English
languages.notes: Medium of education and government working language. No L1 community.

languages.name: Classical Tibetan
languages.notes: Chöke: monastic/religious register. Code xct (Classical Tibetan), NOT bod (modern Standard Tibetan).

languages.name: Bhutanese Sign Language
languages.notes: No distinct ISO code established; young/developing variety. Verify pass 2 (WFD).

countries.notesLongTail: Below-threshold but named (all <25k L1): Bumthangkha kjz, Khengkha xkf, Kurtöpkha xkz, Dzala dzl, Ole ole, Brokkat bro, Lhokpu lhp, Gongduk goe (highly divergent, ~1–2k), Dakpa dka, Chali teh, Dzalakha dzl?, Brokpa. Hindi widely understood via media (no community). No other official languages.

countries.name: India

livingLanguages.note: ≈450 living (Ethnologue ed.25–27 range ≈448–462); census mother-tongue returns (≈19k raw, rationalised to 121 + 22) are NOT a language count

languages.name: Hindi
languages.notes: Union official (Devanagari) + 9 states/UTs. Census 'Hindi' mother-tongue umbrella (≈44%) includes Bhojpuri/Rajasthani/Chhattisgarhi returns — the single biggest counting dispute in Indian linguistics; do not present census Hindi as one variety.

languages.name: English
languages.notes: Associate official (never lapsed). State-official in Nagaland, Meghalaya, Arunachal. L2 estimates range 100–250M — genuinely uncertain.

languages.name: Bengali
languages.notes: 8th Schedule; official in West Bengal, Tripura (and Barak Valley districts of Assam). Classical-language status 2024.

languages.name: Marathi
languages.notes: 8th Schedule; official in Maharashtra. Classical-language status 2024.

languages.name: Telugu
languages.notes: 8th Schedule; official in Andhra Pradesh + Telangana. Classical language.

languages.name: Tamil
languages.notes: 8th Schedule; official in Tamil Nadu (+ Puducherry). First-declared Classical language (2004).

languages.name: Gujarati
languages.notes: 8th Schedule; official in Gujarat (+ DNHDD).

languages.name: Urdu
languages.notes: 8th Schedule; additional-official in UP, Bihar, Jharkhand, Telangana, West Bengal, Delhi. Hindi–Urdu: one grammar continuum, two literary standards — teach together with script notes, never merge silently.

languages.name: Kannada
languages.notes: 8th Schedule; official in Karnataka. Classical language.

languages.name: Odia
languages.notes: 8th Schedule; official in Odisha. Classical language. Renamed Oriya→Odia (2011); code 'ory' unchanged.

ekguru.recommendation: recommended-course — 45M speakers, state-official, zero EkGuru coverage.

languages.name: Malayalam
languages.notes: 8th Schedule; official in Kerala (+ Lakshadweep, Mahe). Classical language.

languages.name: Punjabi (Eastern)
languages.notes: 8th Schedule; official in Punjab (+ Delhi additional). Gurmukhi script. Eastern Punjabi (pan) vs Western Punjabi/Lahnda (pnb, Pakistan) — distinct codes, distinct standards; cross-border note, no merge.

languages.name: Assamese
languages.notes: 8th Schedule; official in Assam. Classical-language status 2024.

ekguru.recommendation: recommended-course — state-official, classical status, NE gateway.

languages.name: Maithili
languages.notes: 8th Schedule; additional-official in Jharkhand. Census undercounts (many returns folded into 'Hindi'); Ethnologue total much higher — dispute preserved, confidence low on numbers only.

languages.name: Santali
languages.notes: 8th Schedule (2003); additional-official in Jharkhand. Only Munda language in the Schedule; Ol Chiki script. Largest tribal language of India.

languages.name: Kashmiri
languages.notes: 8th Schedule; official in J&K (2020 Act, Perso-Arabic + Devanagari scripts notified). Dardic — the Schedule's only Dardic language.

languages.name: Nepali
languages.notes: 8th Schedule (as 'Nepali', macro 'nep'); official in Sikkim + Darjeeling/Kalimpong (WB additional). Individual code npi (Nepal entry) — same language, dual-code treatment documented, not merged.

ekguru.recommendation: recommended-pack — one Nepali pack serves IN+NP+BT.

languages.name: Sindhi
languages.notes: 8th Schedule; official NOWHERE in India (partition dispersal) — the Schedule's only stateless major language. Perso-Arabic + Devanagari scripts.

ekguru.recommendation: recommended-pack — heritage demand, no state machinery to compete with.

languages.name: Dogri
languages.notes: 8th Schedule (2003); official in J&K (2020). Census vs Ethnologue totals differ (Kangri overlap debate) — numbers low-confidence.

languages.name: Konkani
languages.notes: 8th Schedule; official in Goa (Devanagari script mandated). Macrolanguage 'kok' (individual: gom Goan Konkani). Five-script tradition (Devanagari/Roman/Kannada/Malayalam/Perso-Arabic) — script note essential.

languages.name: Bodo
languages.notes: 8th Schedule (2003); associate-official in Assam (2020 Bodo Accord), official in Bodoland Territorial Region. Tibeto-Burman; Devanagari script.

languages.name: Manipuri (Meitei)
languages.notes: 8th Schedule; official in Manipur. 'Manipuri' is the constitutional name, 'Meitei/Meiteilon' the endonym; Meitei Mayek script revival ongoing. Code 'mni' macrolanguage treatment — verify pass 2.

languages.name: Sanskrit
languages.notes: 8th Schedule; 2nd-official in Uttarakhand (+ Himachal). Census L1 (~25k) is symbolic self-report, not a speech community — liturgical/scholarly role is the honest frame. Classical language.

ekguru.recommendation: recommended-pack — liturgical/heritage demand; teach as classical, never as vernacular.

languages.name: Bhojpuri
languages.notes: NOT scheduled (long-standing demand). Census folds most Bhojpuri returns into 'Hindi' — the 50M figure is Ethnologue-side; dispute preserved. Large diaspora (Mauritius, Fiji, Suriname, Guyana, Trinidad).

ekguru.recommendation: recommended-course — 50M+ speakers and diaspora; strongest non-scheduled candidate in India.

languages.name: Indian Sign Language
languages.notes: Code 'ins'. ISLRTC (2015) standardising; no constitutional status. Shared signing family with Pakistan/Bangladesh/Nepal varieties — related, not identical; do not merge (see BD/PK/NP notes).

ekguru.recommendation: watch — video-first medium; EkGuru is text-first today.

countries.notesLongTail: Other 100k+ NOT individually listed (batch scope; scheduled-first): Chhattisgarhi hne (~18M), Magahi mag (~14M), Haryanvi bgc (~13M), Marwari mwr (~8M; Rajasthani macro dispute — verify pass 2), Malvi mup, Mewari mtr, Shekhawati swv, Bundeli bns, Bagheli bfy, Awadhi awa (~4M IN), Braj bjj, Kanauji bjj?, Garhwali gbm, Kumaoni kfy, Mandeali, Kangri xnr, Bhili bhb (~3M; Bhil group), Gondi gon (macro; ~3M), Kokborok trp, Mizo lus (~1M; Mizoram official), Khasi kha (~1.4M; Meghalaya associate-official; Austroasiatic), Garo grt, Mundari unr, Ho hoc, Kurukh kfb, Kharia khr, Nicobarese group, Tulu tcy (~2M; classical-demand), Kodava kfa, Kurumba, Toda txn (~1k, famous), Kota kfe, Badaga bfq, Kannauji, Ladakhi lbj, Balti bft, Shina scl, Burushaski bsk, Khowar khw, Wakhi wbl, Tibetan bod (exile community), Dzongkha dzo (border), Nepali dialects, English creoles (Nagamese nag, Nefamese), Andamanese (Aka-Jeru akj etc., moribund), Humburi? no. Pali pli + Prakrit pra: classical-status 2024, liturgical (Buddhist/Jain) — notes, not entries (no L1). Portuguese por: Goa/Daman heritage (~10k L1?) — historical/minority; Diu/Indo-Portuguese creoles moribund. French fra: Puducherry heritage. Persian fas: historical (Mughal court) — historical role candidate, verify pass 2.

countries.name: Iran

livingLanguages.note: ≈75 living; Turkic varieties (Qashqai, Khorasani) drive the uncertainty

languages.name: Persian
languages.notes: Constitution Art.15: Persian is official. Macrolanguage 'fas'; Iran variety = Western Persian (pes). Dari (prs) and Tajik (tgk) are mutually intelligible standards — one course + notes can serve all three.

ekguru.recommendation: recommended-course — existingfa starter pack exists (Beta); promote to full course. Shared with AF/TJ.

languages.name: South Azerbaijani
languages.notes: Iran's largest minority language (NW + Tehran). South Azerbaijani (azb) vs North Azerbaijani (azj, Azerbaijan republic) — distinct codes; Perso-Arabic vs Latin scripts. Estimates 12–23M — genuinely disputed, low on numbers.

languages.name: Central Kurdish (Sorani)
languages.notes: Kordestan/West Azerbaijan. Kurdish is NOT one code: ckb (Sorani) + kmr (Kurmanji) + sdh (Southern) listed separately per rule 12.

ekguru.recommendation: recommended-pack — shared with IQ (Sorani official-regional there).

languages.name: Northern Kurdish (Kurmanji)
languages.notes: Khorasan + NW pockets. Latin script tradition (vs Sorani Perso-Arabic) — script note essential.

languages.name: Southern Kurdish
languages.notes: Kermanshah/Ilam. Often folded into 'Kurdish' totals — listed separately here.

ekguru.recommendation: watch — pack only if Kurdish cluster funds it.

languages.name: Gilaki
languages.notes: Gilan (Caspian). NW Iranian; not Persian-dialect — distinct language.

languages.name: Mazanderani
languages.notes: Mazandaran (Caspian). Tabari literary tradition.

languages.name: Northern Luri
languages.notes: Lorestan. 'Luri' is two codes (lrc + luz) — listed separately.

languages.name: Southern Luri
languages.notes: Kohgiluyeh/Fars highlands. Includes Bakhtiari varieties per Ethnologue treatment — flag for pass-2 dialect check.

languages.name: Western Balochi
languages.notes: Sistan-Baluchestan. Individual code bgn (vs macro 'bal' in AF entry — AF figure is less certain, hence macro there).

languages.name: Mesopotamian Arabic
languages.notes: Khuzestan Arabs (Ahwaz). Constitution Art.16 mandates Arabic in curriculum (Quranic/educational). Gulf Arabic (acq) also present on the coast — verify pass 2 whether separate entry warranted.

ekguru.recommendation: Covered by MSA course notes; Gulf/Mesopotamian packs only on demand.

languages.name: Turkmen
languages.notes: Golestan (Turkmensahra). Same code as TM/AF Turkmen — cross-border note.

languages.name: Qashqai
languages.notes: Fars confederacy; Oghuz Turkic. Estimates 500k–1.5M; some treatments fold into Azerbaijani — dispute preserved, do not merge.

languages.name: Talysh
languages.notes: Gilan/Ardabil + Azerbaijan republic. NW Iranian.

languages.name: Khorasani Turkish
languages.notes: NE Khorasan Oghuz. Distinct-code treatment (kmz) is Ethnologue-side; endonym often just 'Turki'. Verify pass 2.

languages.name: Armenian
languages.notes: Constitutionally recognised religious minority (Art.13) with schools/press (Isfahan Jolfa, Tehran). Code 'hye' covers both standards here; Western/Eastern split note for AM entry.

ekguru.recommendation: Shared with Armenia entry — one Armenian pack serves both.

languages.name: Assyrian Neo-Aramaic
languages.notes: Recognised minority (Art.13, Urmia). Below 100k but constitutionally recognised → listed per threshold rule. Last Neo-Aramaic community of its size in situ.

languages.name: Persian Sign Language
languages.notes: Code 'psc' established. Distinct from Arabic SLs.

countries.notesLongTail: Below-threshold/notes-only: Tati group (tks?/esh? — Tati is a cluster, pass-2 split), Semnani smy, Sangsari sgr, Caspian Taleshi dialects, Vafsi vaf, Hawrami hac (Kurdish-cluster edge — Gorani; listed under Kurdish dispute), Zazaki? no (Turkey only), Georgian kat (Fereydan, ~50k), Circassian? no, Brahui brh (small pockets), Domari rmt (tiny), Mandaic mid (Khuzestan, ~few hundred speakers, endangered), Hebrew hbo liturgical (Jewish community ~10k), Syriac syc liturgical (Assyrian church). Azeri vs Khalaj klj (Qom, ~40k, arguable Turkic isolate) — notes. Dari/Zoroastrian gbz (~10k, NOT Afghan Dari — name collision flagged!).

countries.name: Sri Lanka

languages.name: Sinhala
languages.notes: Constitution Ch.IV: Sinhala + Tamil official; English the 'link language'. Diglossic (literary vs spoken) — course must teach spoken first.

languages.name: Tamil
languages.notes: Official. Sri Lankan Tamil (Jaffna) vs Indian Tamil (plantation) vs Tamil Nadu Tamil — dialect continuum, one code 'tam'; Jaffna notes essential for a course.

ekguru.recommendation: Course exists — ADD Sri Lankan Tamil notes module (Jaffna lexicon, address terms).

languages.name: English
languages.notes: Constitutional 'link language'; business/education. No significant L1 community.

languages.name: Sri Lankan Creole Malay
languages.notes: Malay community (Colombo/Slave Island). Below 100k but the country's only creole + distinct code → listed per exceptional-case rule. Endangered (shift to Tamil/Sinhala).

languages.name: Vedda
languages.notes: Moribund aboriginal language (Dambana). Whether fluent L1 remains is disputed — possibly rememberers only. Listed as exceptional case (country's only indigenous language).

languages.name: Sri Lankan Sign Language
languages.notes: Code 'sqs'. Distinct from Indian/Pakistani signing.

countries.notesLongTail: Deliberately NOT entries (rule 16): Rodiya (Sinhala sociolect, not a language). Indian Tamil ≈ plantation Tamil — same code 'tam'. Malayalam: small trader community, no entry. Arabic arb liturgical (Muslim education). Portuguese creole (Sri Lanka Portuguese, moribund — 'historical' candidate, verify pass 2). Dutch burgher community shifted to English.

countries.name: Maldives

livingLanguages.note: Dhivehi + established English + MSL(uncertain) — count depends on MSL treatment

languages.name: Dhivehi
languages.notes: Sole official/national language. Thaana script (RTL, Indic+Arabic hybrid). Southern atolls (Addu/Fuvahmulah/Huvadhu/Mulaku) speak divergent varieties — DIALECTS of 'div' per authoritative treatment (rule 16: not separate entries). Closest relative: Sinhala.

ekguru.recommendation: recommended-pack — small authoring surface, tourist demand, script story.

languages.name: English
languages.notes: Education/tourism/government working language. No L1 community.

languages.name: Bengali
languages.notes: Migrant-worker community (construction). Estimates vary widely with labour cycles.

ekguru.recommendation: No action (course exists for other reasons).

languages.name: Maldivian Sign Language
languages.notes: No distinct ISO code established; documentation thin. Verify pass 2 (WFD/Maldives deaf orgs).

countries.notesLongTail: Other worker languages (Sinhala, Tamil, Hindi/Urdu) transient — notes only. Arabic arb liturgical (100% Muslim; Islamic education).

countries.name: Nepal

livingLanguages.note: 124 mother tongues returned in Census 2021 (census categories, exact-ish); Ethnologue lists ≈130 living — two counts, both kept

languages.name: Nepali
languages.notes: Federal official (Devanagari). Individual code 'npi'; India's scheduled entry uses macro 'nep' — SAME language, dual-code treatment documented (rule 12). All mother tongues are constitutionally 'national languages' (Art.7) — symbolic status, not function.

ekguru.recommendation: recommended-course — federal-official, 16M, cross-border (IN/BT), zero EkGuru coverage.

languages.name: Maithili
languages.notes: Official in Madhesh Province (2021, with Bhojpuri). Bajjika (≈800k returns) is counted by many linguists as Maithili — NOT a separate entry (rule 16), noted here. Tirhuta/Mithilakshar script heritage; Devanagari in practice.

languages.name: Bhojpuri
languages.notes: Official in Madhesh Province (2021). Nepal figure is census-clean (unlike India's Hindi-folded count).

languages.name: Tharu languages
languages.notes: Census category 'Tharu' covers Dangaura (thl), Rana (thr), Kathoriya and others — a cluster, hence group entry. CAREFUL: thl (Dangaura Tharu) vs ths (Thakali) — different languages, similar codes.

ekguru.recommendation: watch — cluster needs dialect survey before any pack.

languages.name: Tamang languages
languages.notes: Census 'Tamang' covers Eastern (taj) + Western (tdg) — distinct codes, hence group entry. Tamyig script heritage.

languages.name: Newar
languages.notes: Kathmandu Valley (Nepal Bhasa). Bagmati-province recognition reported — NOT confirmed as official function; kept 'regional' + note (honest downgrade, verify pass 2). Ranjana/Prachalit scripts.

languages.name: Magar languages
languages.notes: Census 'Magar' covers Eastern (mgp) + Western (mrd) — distinct codes, group entry.

languages.name: Awadhi
languages.notes: Western Terai (Lumbini). Larger community in UP, India (folded into Hindi census there).

ekguru.recommendation: watch — Awadhi pack would be IN+NP shared; demand unproven.

languages.name: Doteli
languages.notes: Far-west (Doti). Distinct code from Nepali — the 'Nepali dialect' claim is folk-political, not linguistic.

languages.name: Urdu
languages.notes: Terai Muslim communities. Cross-border standard with IN/PK.

languages.name: Limbu
languages.notes: Kirat east (Taplejung/Panchthar). Sirijanga script. Koshi-province recognition reported — unverified, kept regional.

languages.name: Gurung languages
languages.notes: Census 'Gurung/Tamu'; Western (gvr) + Eastern varieties — Eastern split treatment uncertain (pass 2). Single-member group for now, flagged.

languages.name: Bantawa
languages.notes: Largest Rai (Kirat) variety; other Rai languages (Chamling rab ~70k, etc.) below threshold — notes. 'Rai' is an ethnicity, not a language (rule 15).

languages.name: Rajbanshi
languages.notes: Jhapa/Morang Koch-Rajbanshi. Rangpuri/Kamtapuri continuum dispute (IN/BD) — code treatment verify pass 2.

languages.name: Sherpa
languages.notes: Everest region; trekking-world famous. Sambhota script use growing.

ekguru.recommendation: recommended-pack — trekker demand is real and monetisable.

languages.name: Hindi
languages.notes: Terai lingua franca via media/schooling; small L1 base in Nepal. No official status.

languages.name: English
languages.notes: Education/administration working language. No L1 community.

languages.name: Nepali Sign Language
languages.notes: Code 'nsp' established. Kathmandu-based standard; legal recognition process ongoing (verify pass 2).

countries.notesLongTail: Other-province official-designation claims (Koshi Maithili/Limbu, Bagmati Tamang/Newar, Lumbini Tharu/Awadhi) UNVERIFIED — deliberately not 'official-regional' until pass 2 confirms function, not announcement. Below-threshold/notes-only: Sunuwar suz (~40k), Chamling rab (~70k), other Rai (~30 codes), Dhimal dhi, Meche, Jirel jul, Yolmo scp, Mugom, Kaike, Dolpo, Loke, Nubri, Tsum, Manangba, Nar-Phu, Thakali ths (~10k — NOT thl!), Baram brd (moribund), Kusunda kgg (isolate, ~30 speakers, famous), Raji rji, Raute rau (nomadic, ~150), Kisan, Bhujel, Dura ddr (extinct 2022? — verify; 'extinct' candidate), Waling, Bajjika (see Maithili note), Angika anp, Musasa? no. Sanskrit san: liturgical/education. Pali: Buddhist liturgical (Lumbini).

countries.name: Pakistan

languages.name: Urdu
languages.notes: Constitution Art.251: Urdu national language; English official 'until replaced' (never replaced). Mother-tongue ≈10% (Muhajir/Karachi) but universal L2 — the L1-vs-total gap is the honest story.

languages.name: English
languages.notes: De-jure official alongside Urdu; courts/higher education. No L1 community.

languages.name: Western Panjabi
languages.notes: Pakistan's largest mother tongue (≈37% per census) — and official NOWHERE, not even in Punjab province. Western Panjabi/Lahnda (pnb, Shahmukhi) vs Eastern Punjabi (pan, Gurmukhi, India): distinct codes AND scripts — cross-border note, no merge.

ekguru.recommendation: recommended-course — 80M+ speakers, zero official machinery, zero EkGuru coverage. Shahmukhi script.

languages.name: Sindhi
languages.notes: Official in Sindh (with Urdu). Perso-Arabic script (52 letters).

languages.name: Saraiki
languages.notes: South Punjab (Multan/Bahawalpur). Separate census category since 1981; 'Punjabi dialect' claim is political, not linguistic — distinct code stands. Provincehood movement uses language identity.

ekguru.recommendation: recommended-course — 25M, distinct identity, no EkGuru coverage.

languages.name: Northern Pashto
languages.notes: KP + north Balochistan + Karachi (Pashtun ≈15% of Pakistan). Census 'Pashto' covers pbu (Northern, Yusufzai/Peshawar) + pbt (Southern pockets) + pst (Waziristan Central?) — split estimates uncertain; pbu listed as dominant with pbt/pst in note (AF entry covers the cluster as group).

ekguru.recommendation: recommended-pack — shared planning with AF Pashto group.

languages.name: Balochi
languages.notes: Macrolanguage 'bal': Pakistan holds Western (bgn, Rakhshani), Southern (bcc, coastal) and Eastern (bgp, Derajat). Census 'Balochi' ≈3.7% but undercounts Brahui-adjacent returns — dispute noted.

ekguru.recommendation: recommended-pack — bgn base with bcc/bgp notes.

languages.name: Southern Hindko
languages.notes: Hazara/Peshawar valley. Lahnda cluster: hnd (Southern) + hno (Northern) are distinct codes — listed separately (rule 12), numbers uncertain.

ekguru.recommendation: watch — pack only if Lahnda cluster (pnb/skr/hnd) funds together.

languages.name: Northern Hindko
languages.notes: Hazara highlands (Mansehra/Battagram). See hnd note.

languages.name: Brahui
languages.notes: Dravidian language 1500km from its family (Kalat). Census folds many Brahui returns into 'Balochi' — count disputed, listed separately regardless (rule 12).

languages.name: Gujari
languages.notes: Gujjar community (AJK/north Punjab/KP). Rajasthani-family; distinct from Gujarati (guj) — name-similarity trap flagged.

languages.name: Khowar
languages.notes: Chitral lingua franca (Dardic). Perso-Arabic script, growing literature.

languages.name: Shina
languages.notes: Gilgit-Baltistan main language (Dardic). Kohistani Shina vs Gilgit Shina dialect spread — one code.

languages.name: Balti
languages.notes: Baltistan (Tibetic, Perso-Arabic script — rare combination). Purki/Purigi (India) closely related.

languages.name: Burushaski
languages.notes: LANGUAGE ISOLATE (Hunza/Nagar) — unrelated to anything on Earth. Dialects: Hunza/Nagar/Yasin (Yasin divergent — pass-2 split check).

ekguru.recommendation: recommended-pack — isolate-celebrity value outweighs small base.

languages.name: Kashmiri
languages.notes: AJK (Neelum Valley) + diaspora. Small vs Indian side (7M). Cross-border note with IN entry.

ekguru.recommendation: Shared with India Kashmiri pack — no separate action.

languages.name: Memoni
languages.notes: Memon community (Karachi; Kathiawad origin). Gujarati-family. Dual role: historic migrants, now multi-generation minority.

languages.name: Standard Arabic
languages.notes: Quranic/madrassa Arabic; no L1 community.

ekguru.recommendation: Covered by MSA Arabic course notes.

languages.name: Pakistani Sign Language
languages.notes: Code 'pks'. ISL-family related (shared history with Indian signing) — distinct national variety, not coded 'ins'.
